extracted.intended_audience: scholars of humor, rhetoric, and performance studies; theorists of stand-up comedy; advanced students and researchers interested in comedic argumentation
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating stand-up jokes and performances as acts of rhetorical argument — assessing whether and how they advance a comic worldview, persuade an audience, and deploy rhetorical appeals and timing. Focuses on coherence of stance, audience negotiation, and rhetorical techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stand-up as rhetorical discourse
rubrics_metrics.description: "Stand-up comedy is inherently rhetorical discourse: it strives not only to entertain, but to persuade..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat stand-up not merely as entertainment but as argumentation. Evaluate whether the performance attempts to convince the audience to adopt a particular comic vision or worldview; consider persuasion as an explicit aim alongside humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jokes assert claims about the world
rubrics_metrics.description: "Every joke makes a claim about the world."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether individual jokes put forward a proposition or interpretation of reality. Identify the claim being made and whether it coheres with other claims in the set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the joke advance a coherent comic vision?
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit rubric item: "Does the joke advance a coherent comic vision?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for accumulation and consistency across jokes: do they build toward a recognizable perspective or worldview? Evaluate internal coherence, recurring themes, and whether new jokes reinforce or contradict the established vision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the rhetorical stance clear?
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit rubric item: "Is the rhetorical stance clear?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the comedian's persona/stance (their ethical/ideological position, persona, or attitude) is intelligible to the audience. A clear stance helps listeners map jokes onto the comic vision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the audience implicitly persuaded (audience consent)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit rubric item: "Is the audience implicitly persuaded?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate signs that the audience accepts the claim (laughs as consent). Consider implicit persuasion: does the set move audience attitudes without explicit argument? Contrast genuine persuasion with mere noise or nervous laughter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of rhetorical appeals: ethos, pathos, logos, kairos
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit rubric item: "Does it use ethos / pathos / logos / kairos?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check how the performance employs: ethos (comedian's persona/credibility), pathos (emotional connection, shared experience), logos (surprising logical inversions or reasoning), and kairos (timing and topical relevance). Note examples of each and their effectiveness for the specific audience/context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laughter as signal of agreement, not just relief
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit rubric item: "Does laughter signal genuine agreement, not just relief?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate types of laughter—assess whether laughter indicates acceptance of the comic claim or is merely a physiological/relief response. Use contextual cues (applause, follow-up reactions, silence) to interpret the meaning of laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility of the comic vision / overcoming resistance
rubrics_metrics.description: From 'Audience Negotiation': "Comic's vision must be accessible. Must overcome resistance to the worldview."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the material is framed so that the audience can grasp and adopt the comic perspective. Consider cultural references, explanatory setup, and rhetorical moves that bridge gaps between performer and audience; note where resistance remains unaddressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funniness as audience-specific persuasive power
rubrics_metrics.description: From 'Why It Matters': "Funniness = persuasive power for that audience."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate funniness relative to the intended or actual audience: what counts as funny depends on whether the performance successfully persuades that audience of its comic claims. Ask 'funny to whom?' and consider demographic, cultural, and situational factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience specificity and kairotic/contextual factors
rubrics_metrics.description: From discussions of kairos and audience negotiation: "Different audiences = different rhetorical contexts."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess contextual fit: topicality, timing, current events, and local cultural knowledge determine whether rhetorical moves succeed. Consider whether jokes are opportunely timed and tailored to the occasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stance consistency and identity-construction across jokes
rubrics_metrics.description: From 'Comic Culture': "Each comic establishes a 'stance.' Jokes consistent with the stance accumulate. Identity-construction is ongoing."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the consistency of persona and how repeated jokes construct and reinforce the performer's identity. Note when inconsistency undermines credibility or when accumulation strengthens the comic worldview.
